summary: A personal form builder on your own server: create forms and fields in an admin, publish each at a public URL that works without JavaScript, store answers in SQLite with file uploads on disk, get an email or webhook per response, and export CSV. Your respondents' data stays in your file.

stack.why: many routes and forms; a thin framework earns its place here
public forms must submit with JavaScript disabled
one server, one disk, simple backups

prerequisites.name: Node.js 22 or newer
prerequisites.why: Everything in this build runs on it: the server, the scripts, the tests.
prerequisites.get: Download the LTS installer from nodejs.org, or install with your package manager (brew install node, or nvm install 22). Restart the terminal afterwards.

prerequisites.name: A terminal and a code editor
prerequisites.why: Every step below is a command you type or a file you edit.
prerequisites.get: VS Code (code.visualstudio.com), Cursor or Zed. Open a folder for the project and use the editor's built-in terminal.
prerequisites.verify: You can open a folder and run a command in its terminal

prerequisites.name: Git
prerequisites.why: History for your code, and the way most hosts deploy.
prerequisites.get: Install from git-scm.com or with your package manager, then run git init in the project folder once it exists.

prerequisites.name: One long random admin token
prerequisites.why: The admin is protected by a single token, no user accounts.
prerequisites.get: openssl rand -base64 32 into .env as ADMIN_TOKEN. Store it in your password manager.

prerequisites.name: SMTP credentials for response notifications (optional)
prerequisites.why: Phase 7 emails you each response. Any SMTP provider works; without one, use the webhook or just read the admin.
prerequisites.get: Fastmail, Postmark, Resend or your mail host: create an app password or SMTP credential, note host, port, user, password.

prerequisites.name: A webhook URL to receive responses (optional)
prerequisites.why: The other notification path: a Zapier or Make hook, or webhook.site while testing.
prerequisites.get: Create one at webhook.site to test with; replace with the real target later.

prerequisites.name: A small always-on server (VPS)
prerequisites.why: This needs one process running all the time with a public address. Uploads need disk that persists across deploys.
prerequisites.get: Hetzner Cloud (from about 4 EUR), DigitalOcean or Fly.io. Ubuntu 24.04, the smallest size. You need SSH access and a public IP. Only needed for the deploy phase; develop locally first.

prerequisites.name: A domain or subdomain
prerequisites.why: A public address you own, so links you share never break when a provider changes.
prerequisites.get: Register at Cloudflare Registrar, Porkbun or Namecheap, or use a subdomain of one you already own. You add one DNS record in the deploy phase.
prerequisites.cost: roughly $10 a year, or free on an existing domain

prerequisites.name: Caddy on the server
prerequisites.why: Automatic HTTPS in front of the Node process. Without TLS the browser features this relies on (and your visitors' trust) do not work.
prerequisites.get: On the VPS: follow the install steps at caddyserver.com/docs/install for Ubuntu. One Caddyfile with your domain and a reverse_proxy line is the whole config.
prerequisites.verify: caddy version prints a version on the server

env.name: UPLOAD_DIR
env.where: Where files land, per form slug.

env.name: ADMIN_TOKEN
env.where: openssl rand -base64 32. The only admin credential.

env.name: SMTP_URL
env.where: SMTP connection string from your provider.

phases.title: Form definition and admin auth
phases.goal: An admin you can log into with the token, and forms you can create.

steps.do: Create the project and the tables
steps.detail: forms (id, slug, title, description, accent, published, notify_email, webhook_url), fields (id, form_id, position, kind, label, help, required, options JSON, deleted), responses (id, form_id, submitted_at, ip_hash, user_agent_class), answers (id, response_id, field_id, value, file_path).
commands: mkdir forms && cd forms && git init && npm init -y && npm pkg set type=module

steps.do: Implement token login
steps.detail: POST the token; compare with a constant-time function; set an HttpOnly cookie. Never accept the token in a URL.

steps.do: Build form CRUD in /admin

check: A wrong token is refused
A right one persists across a page load as a cookie
The token never appears in a URL or a log line
A form can be created, renamed and deleted

phases.title: Field editor
phases.goal: Every field kind, reorderable, soft-deleted so old responses keep rendering.

steps.do: Add, edit and soft-delete fields with up/down buttons for order
steps.detail: Kinds: text, textarea, email, select, checkbox, file. Explicit buttons work on mobile and are testable; drag can come later.

steps.do: Store select options as JSON and validate them on save
steps.detail: At least one option, no duplicates, trimmed.

check: A form with one of every kind saves and reloads identically
Reordering persists
A soft-deleted field disappears from the public form but still shows in past responses

phases.title: Public form rendering
phases.goal: Accessible, single column, works without JavaScript, unpublished forms 404.

steps.do: Build GET /f/:slug
steps.detail: Labels with for attributes, one question per block, single column, mobile-first. Unpublished forms return 404.

steps.do: Add the accent custom property, dark mode and a designed thank-you page
steps.detail: prefers-color-scheme with the same custom properties overridden.

check: No accessibility violations
Every field keyboard reachable with a focus ring
Submitting with JavaScript disabled works
An unpublished slug returns 404

phases.title: Submission and validation
phases.goal: Validate on the server against the stored definitions and never lose what someone typed.

steps.do: Implement POST /f/:slug with server-side validation against the stored fields
steps.detail: Required, email shape, select values drawn from the stored options, length caps. Never trust the client copy of the rules.

steps.do: Preserve every typed value on a validation error
steps.detail: Re-render with inline errors and the answers intact; losing a long answer is the worst thing this app can do.

steps.do: Store one answers row per field with the field_id
steps.detail: So a renamed or soft-deleted field still renders in past responses.

check: A valid submission stores one response with one answer per field
An invalid one re-renders with every typed value intact
A forged select value outside the stored options is rejected

phases.title: File uploads
phases.goal: Safe uploads: streamed, capped, sniffed, stripped.

steps.do: Stream multipart to UPLOAD_DIR/<slug>/ under a generated name
steps.detail: Cap at MAX_UPLOAD_MB while streaming; check MIME against the decoded header; strip EXIF from images with sharp.

steps.do: Never serve UPLOAD_DIR directly; serve via an admin-only route

check: An oversize file is refused before it is fully read
A .php renamed to .png is refused
Two uploads with the same original name coexist
Uploads are not reachable without admin auth

phases.title: Spam controls
phases.goal: Honeypot, minimum fill time, per-IP limits in SQLite.

steps.do: Add a CSS-hidden honeypot and a signed minimum-fill timestamp requiring 3 seconds
Rate limit 10 submissions per IP per hour in a SQLite table

check: A filled honeypot shows thanks and stores nothing
A sub-3-second submission is refused
The eleventh in an hour is refused while another IP succeeds

phases.title: Notifications and export
phases.goal: Email and webhook that can never make a respondent wait, and a streamed CSV.

steps.do: Send email over SMTP_URL and POST the webhook, fire-and-forget with a timeout
Build the admin response table and streamed CSV export

check: A submission still stores and shows thanks with SMTP unreachable and the webhook timing out
A real email arrives readable on a phone
A 10,000-row CSV exports without memory growth

phases.title: Deploy
phases.goal: Live, backed up including uploads, documented.

steps.do: Add /healthz, systemd, Caddy and a backup of data/
Write the README
steps.detail: .env keys, the Caddy snippet, where the database and uploads live, and the honest line that Tally's free tier is generous and the reason to build this is data ownership.

check: A restore brings back both responses and files
A reader goes from clone to a published form using only the README

phases.title: Operate it like a product
phases.goal: Only for the product-builder path: know when the form server is down, never lose the database, and keep the server patched.

steps.do: Add a /healthz endpoint and an external uptime check against it
steps.detail: Answer 200 with the build id and a quick database read. Point a free uptime monitor (or your own, from the Healthchecks entry on this site) at it so an outage is noticed before a user notices.

steps.do: Write structured request logs and rotate them
steps.detail: One JSON line per request: method, path, status, duration, no raw IPs. Rotate weekly with logrotate, keep eight.

steps.do: Back the SQLite file up off the machine nightly and test a restore
steps.detail: SQLite's .backup command makes a consistent copy while the app runs. Copy it to object storage or a second machine; then, once, restore it into a fresh checkout and confirm the app reads it.

steps.do: Lock the box down
steps.detail: Firewall allowing only 22, 80 and 443; unattended security updates on; the app running as an unprivileged user under systemd with Restart=on-failure.

check: Stopping the service triggers an uptime alert within a few minutes
A restore from last night's backup contains yesterday's data
A port scan from another machine shows only 22, 80 and 443

product.outcome: A form service for one person or a small team: any number of forms, uploads handled safely, respondent data never leaving your server.

architecture.owns: token auth, form and field CRUD
architecture.swap: Add real accounts later behind the same routes
A JavaScript-enhanced form could sit on top; the POST contract stays
Object storage behind the same write/read functions

operations.backup: tar of data/ nightly off the box.
operations.restore: Extract, start, check one form and one upload.
operations.monitoring: Uptime on /healthz; alert on a spike in refused submissions.
operations.incident: Spam wave: tighten limits, bulk-delete. Compromise: rebuild, restore data/, rotate ADMIN_TOKEN and SMTP credentials.

releaseGate: Every validation path verified with a fixture
Upload rejection verified with a fake image and an oversize file
One restore drill including uploads performed and dated
Notifications verified fire-and-forget with SMTP down

notIncluded: Team workspaces and custom domains per form.
after: Conditional visibility for one field based on another's value
